target_customer: Healthcare startups and providers that need insurance eligibility checks and billing through an API
problem: Checking eligibility and filing claims with insurers is fragmented and hard to automate for small developers.
business_model: Usage-based API for insurance eligibility, claims and billing

founders.name: Katelyn Gleason
founders.background_notes: YC page cites Forbes 30 Under 30 in Healthcare and Fast Company recognition but gives no prior employers or education.

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapping many payer connections and formats into one REST API is integration-heavy but uses established standards.

defensibility.rationale: Payer connections and customer integrations create stickiness, though established clearinghouses offered similar services.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows these incumbents buying or copying Eligible; current comparison pages list modern API rivals such as Redox and pVerify, which emerged later.

market_need_then: A 2013 HIT Consultant profile covered Eligible's REST API as an effort to standardize eligibility requests to insurers, indicating a known pain point; no spending data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses the exact domain eligible.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer-oriented, billing platform built for builders per its YC page.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder press recognition from Forbes, Fast Company and Business Insider is cited on the YC page; no community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A fitting one-word name with a registered trademark, but little evidence of recognition outside founder press.

outcome_analysis: Eligible built an eligibility and billing API, raised about 2.3 million dollars per an SEC filing reported in 2015, and went quiet in public after about 2017. It is still listed as active with a status page, but company claims of over 25 million raised are not supported by filings, so its trajectory is unclear.
notes: Company site returned 403 to fetch. A third-party review reportedly finds Form D sales totaling 2,682,896 dollars against a company claim of over 25M raised; the 25M is unverified and not recorded as a round. The 2.3M round is dated by article year only, and stage is not stated so it is other. Sources disagree on founding year (2011 vs 2012) and total funding (15M to 27.9M). Search summaries called Gleason co-founder in one place but the YC page lists only her. No dated 2012 competitor sources were found; Availity and Change Healthcare appeared only in current vendor pages.
